name: American Economic Review
description: Manuscripts for the American Economic Review: 11-point type with spacing of 1.5 and one-inch margins, the layout by which the journal measures length; sections numbered in roman numerals, footnotes, no title page, and an abstract of 100 words or fewer.

source.name: American Economic Association, AER Submission Guidelines, Style Guide, and Accepted Articles: Manuscript Preparation Guidelines
source.notes: The style guide is required for accepted articles and optional at submission. Margins, type size and line spacing are not rules in themselves: they are the layout in which the journal states its recommended length, '40 pages when formatted using 11-point font, 1.5 spacing, and 1-inch margins, or 45 pages when formatted using 12-point font' (the first is entered). Not specified, and taken from the general default: typeface, alignment, paragraph indent, hyphenation, the typographic form of headings, block quotations, size and spacing of notes, the heading and layout of the reference list (the source speaks of 'references'; 'References' is entered), page numbers, keywords, line numbers. The page size is not stated: letter was chosen for a North American journal. Headings are numbered in outline form, roman numerals for main sections and capital letters for the first subsections; numbering here is in the application's own form. The introduction has no heading. There is no title page: title, byline and affiliations stand at the top of the first page, with a footnote of acknowledgement. The source does not speak of anonymisation. Appendices in the paper come before the references. Reference style: 'Chicago Manual Author-Date', the edition not named. Submission as PDF.

limits.note: The limit is stated in pages: it is strongly recommended that manuscripts not exceed 40 pages in 11-point type, or 45 in 12-point, with 1.5 spacing and 1-inch margins, figures, tables, references and appendices included. Abstract of 100 words or fewer.
